verdicts.reason: A has a clear top-to-bottom story (product, headline, subcopy, CTA), but the CTA is centred under left-aligned text, and the logo is shrunk into the bottom-left corner close to the edge. In B the one-line headline runs nearly to the right edge and is jammed under the logo, which sits on top of the decorative circle. B's product floats in the middle with a big empty gap above the CTA, so the text block, product and button feel like separate fragments.

Both use the same structure, with left-aligned headline and subcopy above a centred CTA, so the alignment axes clash in both. A tucks the logo into the bottom-left corner as an afterthought. B keeps the logo at top centre as in the original, but crams it against the product's sun icon and leaves dead space under the CTA. B is slightly more faithful to the brand.

In A the headline is pushed against the top and right edges over the busy circle, and the CTA comes before the product, which breaks the reading order. A's product floats alone in the middle and the logo is exiled to the bottom. B reads in a sensible order (product, headline, subcopy, CTA); its flaws are the left-aligned text over a centred button and a small logo crammed into the bottom-left corner.
